title: Exact Optimal Power for Weak-Null Tests in Balanced Completely Randomized Experiments

tldr: For every even \(n\) and positive effect threshold \(k\), deterministic exact rational LP optimization evaluates \(B_{\mathrm{CRE},n}(k)\), returns an attaining total joint-count test of weak-null size at most \(1/20\), and supplies compatible fixed-table mixtures proving the matching bound against all original-record randomized tests. The integer kernel has \(O(n^5)\) entries of \(O(n)\) bits; lexicographic face selection and exact basis recovery give polynomial bit complexity and \(O(n^3)\)-bit basic coordinates. This computational improvement is generic LP theory. It does not select contacts from exchange geometry, resolve the contact-construction question, or establish the original field-level contribution. All heterogeneous nulls and higher-effect alternatives remain in the game.
gap: Existing exact binary randomization inference calibrates prescribed procedures. The inspected papers do not evaluate the fixed-quota all-test guaranteed-power frontier. Finite minimax duality supplies existence, while the contact geometry needed for an explicit structural evaluator remains unresolved.
fill: Construct a rational recursion from quota-preserving mixed differences to compatible contacts and a matching joint-count rule. Evaluate the full finite frontier, its information and design costs, and prospective power under the same effect-only alternative class.
